Diagnosis:
The testPrimitiveTypeClassSerialization test is failing because SerializationUtils.clone throws a ClassNotFoundException when cloning primitive class objects such as int.class or void.class.

Looking at SerializationUtils.clone, the method serializes the object then deserializes it using a custom ClassLoaderAwareObjectInputStream that attempts to resolve classes during deserialization by calling Class.forName with the current classloader or fallback context classloader.

Primitive classes like int.class are not normal serializable classes and cannot be found by Class.forName with their usual names (e.g. "int"). During deserialization, the resolveClass method calls Class.forName with the name of the primitive type, which leads to ClassNotFoundException because primitive types are not loadable by Class.forName.

This root cause is consistent with the bug report which states that cloning a primitive class reference throws ClassNotFoundException. It also explains why the test fails when checking that the cloned class equals the original primitive class.

In summary, the bug is that the deserialization code in ClassLoaderAwareObjectInputStream.resolveClass does not handle primitive types specially. It uses Class.forName for all class names, but Class.forName cannot load names of primitive types.

Hence the failure occurs in the resolveClass method due to the lack of handling for primitive types, causing deserialization to fail and throwing ClassNotFoundException when cloning classes representing primitive types.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
